questions.stem: How does acid rain affect lake ecosystems?

options.text: It makes the water warmer, causing fish to thrive
It lowers the pH, kills fish, and releases toxic aluminium from surrounding soil into the water
It increases the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water
It only affects plants, not animals

questions.explanation: Acid rain lowers the pH of lakes. Most fish die when pH drops below 4.5. Additionally, the acid dissolves aluminium from the surrounding soil, which washes into the lake and is toxic to fish (damaging their gills). Food chains are disrupted and biodiversity decreases, potentially making the lake lifeless.
